FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Surgical Dressings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. This standard was first published in 1984. The first revision of this standard has been taken up to align it with British Pharmacopoeia in respect of the requirement of X-ray -opacity which was not specified in the earlier version. X-ray detectable gauze swabs and laparotomy sponges are widely used items in operation theatres The presence of X-ray detectable member enables them to be located in case of of hospitals. their being left inside the body accidentally. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

5.1 The gauze swabs shall be made by folding the absorbent gauze to the required size in such a way that the free edges do no%:protrcude from the sides. The X-ray detectable member shall be suitably fixed `to the internal folds of the gauze in a longitudinal direction. The maximum off-fold or the misalignment for an individual swab shall not be more than 0.5 cm. It shall be clean and Free ,from physical damage. 5.2 In case .of laparotomy sponges, the swabs shall be made by folding the absorbent gauze to the required size and then stitching on all four sides with loose ends folded inwards. The X-ray detectable member shall be suitably placed atrthe centre of the fold at one corner and stitched from all the sides. A suitable braided cotton ta,pe may be attached at one end df the laparotomy sponge ( the recommended width and length of braided cotton tape is 10 mm and 300 mm, respectively ). The #maximum off-fold or misalignment of the fold shall not be more than IO mm. The swab which shall be clean and free from physical damage, shall also be stitched with two cross stitches at the centre of the swab, parallel to the sides. 5.3 The X-ray detectable member shall be properly anchored to the gauze. It shall show no sign of damage or brittleness. 5.4 The length of the X-ray detectable member shall be according to the size of the swab. It shall be along the entire length of the swab. The thickness of the X-ray detectable member shall not be less than 0.5 mm. 5.5 The absorbent gauze used in gauze swabs and laparotomy sponges shall conform to the requirements given in Table 1. 1

10150 : 1981 3 MATERIAL

3.1 X-ray detectable gauze swabs .and laparotomy sp0nge.s shall consist .of folded absorbent gauze, to which is attached a non-toxic and distinctively coloured monofilament or multiThe filament X-ray d&actable member. absorbent gauze shall consist of cotton cloth of plain or leno `weaves, bleached to white, clean and reasonably free from weaving defects, cotton leaf and shell. The gauze shall be almost odourless. -The X-ray detectable member shall be distinctively coloured and reasonably free from loose fibres and particles; when attached, it shall not impair the softness or flexibility of the gauze.
NOTE - The X-ray detectable membx consists of not less than 55 percent of barium sulphate or a quantity of any other suitable material giving a comparable X-ray opaciiy.

6 OPACITY 6.1 The gauge swabs and laparotomy sponges shall satisfy the test for X-ray opacity in accordance with the method specified in British Pharmacopoeia, Ed. 1988, Vol II, Appendix XXR, ( pA 228 ). 7 STERILIZATION 7.1 If the product is to be supplied in sterilized condition, it may be sterilized by any suitable method of sterilization in accordance with IS 10150 : 1981. 7.1.1 The swabs and withthe test (p 917 ) in 1973. sterilized X-ray detectable gauze laparotomy sponges shall comply for sterility described in Apendix 2% of British Pharmaceutical Codex,

c) Overall dimensions and number of plies of the absorbent gauze (folded ) and quantity; d) Batch/lot number and date of manufacture; e) Indication of the source of manufacture; f) The country of manufacture; and g) If sterilized, it shall be descri!)ed as `STERILIZED Sterility guaranteed unless the pack is opened or damaged'. 9 PACKING 9.1 The X-ray detectable gauze swabs and laparotomy sponges shall be packed in either well-closed packages or sealed pa-ckages according to the requirements of the user. The wax paper shall not be used for any wrapping as it affects the absorbency of the gauze. 9.1.1 If the material is sterilized, it shall be enclosed in a sealed package which is adequate to maintain the sterility of the material up to the time of opening the package.
